title: "Reference: plot functions"

[1 · Initialization and classes](../api.qmd) · [2 · Solvers](../solvers.qmd) · [3 · Getters and saved results](getters.qmd) · **4 · Plot functions**.

Import functions from `PRESS.visualization`. Every plot returns **`(figure, axes)`**, draws observed tracking and consumes previously computed outputs. Plotting never runs a model, selects a new outcome or changes stored probabilities.

```python
from PRESS.visualization import plot_frame, plot_pass_map

fig, ax = plot_frame(press, frame_id, show=False)
fig.savefig("frame.png", dpi=160)

fig, ax = plot_pass_map(
    press, frame_id, field="pass_success",
    pass_target=observed_destination_xy, show=False,
)
fig.savefig("pass_probability.png", dpi=160)
```

## Shared options

The pitch functions accept `pitch_length=None`, `pitch_width=None`, `figsize=(12,8)`, `title_fontsize=9`, `legend_fontsize=8`, plus keyword-only `title=None`, `ax=None`, `show=True`, `legend=True`, `velocity_scale=1.5`. Choice convenience functions retain their original title-size defaults. An explicit axis supports multi-panel figures; its figure is returned. `show=False` supports scripts and batch saving. Plot dimensions use native tracking metadata unless overridden for display.

Velocity arrows are drawing aids of length `velocity_scale × velocity`, not future trajectories. They can be hidden with `velocity_scale=0`. No player-number labels or extra carrier markers are added. Missing players are omitted; a frame without a carrier can still be drawn with `plot_frame`.

## Frames and scalar risks

| Function | Contents |
|---|---|
| `plot_frame(press, frame_id, ..., title=None)` | Players, observed ball and velocity arrows. No prediction is required. |
| `plot_action_selection(press, frame_id, ...)` | Same observed frame with stored native `P(pass)` in the title. |
| `plot_risk(press, frame_id, *, field="hazard", ...)` | Same frame with stored `h`, `residual_risk` or `xloss` in the title. Requires that output to have been computed. |
| `plot_ball_drive_risk(press, frame_id, ...)` | Defender colors show their cause-specific loss probability divided by total drive loss, on a fixed 0–100% scale. Absolute loss appears in the title; zero loss gives zero shares. Defender IDs preserve the correct association when players are missing. |

[Ball-drive example](../vignettes/01_ball_drive_risk/01_ball_drive_risk.ipynb) · [Action-choice example](../vignettes/04_action_selection/04_action_selection.ipynb) · [Case studies](../vignettes/07_case_studies/07_case_studies.ipynb).

## Pass fields

```python
plot_pass_map(press, frame_id, ..., field="pass_success", pass_target=None)
```

| `field` | Stored values and visual scale |
|---|---|
| `pitch_control` | Raw attacking control, absolute probabilities 0–1. |
| `pass_success` | Isotonic-calibrated pass completion, absolute probabilities 0–1. |
| `pass_selection` | Conditional destination-choice distribution. Colors are `100 × cell probability / largest cell probability`, labelled **Relative pass preference (% of maximum)**. |

The relative scale changes only the display: stored destination probabilities still sum to one. Interpolation is solely for rendering. Very small/collinear grids are displayed as colored target points rather than an undefined interpolated surface.

`pass_target=(x,y)` overlays a dashed line from the observed ball to the supplied destination in native centred metres. The destination is supplied by the caller, not inferred by the plot.

`plot_ppcf(...)` remains a compatibility name with `field="pitch_control"` by default. `plot_pass_selection(...)` selects `field="pass_selection"`. Both return figure and axes and accept the common plotting options.

[Pass-probability example](../vignettes/02_pass_probability/02_pass_probability.ipynb) · [Pass-selection example](../vignettes/03_pass_selection/03_pass_selection.ipynb).

## BCOS

`plot_bcos(press_or_bcos, frame_id, ...)` draws the stored probability field and real tracking on an absolute 0–1 scale. It accepts either the match object after `press.compute_bcos(...)` or the standalone `BCOS` object after its own calculation. It does not aggregate an entire match or infer a goal-related interpretation. [BCOS example](../vignettes/spatial_features/bcos/10_bcos.ipynb).
